text_to_speech: Hi gamers, I have an interview with the designers of Terra Mystica. Terra Mystica, like we pronouce in portuguese. It's my pleasure to be here with Helge and Jens. - Jens? - Jens. The designers. And I gonna ask some questions for you. In Brazil we have a lot of fans of your work. Me included. First of all, congrats for the prize. The Deutcher Spielepreis. Did you have expected to win this prize? How was that? We hoped to win it, of course. For me it was no surprise. But how was to receive this award? It was a great feeling yesterday, there was a ceremony, so we enjoyed very much. It was a very great evening, when we got the prize, with all the show. Terra Mystica, I think, had many challenges to develop the game. - Yes. Because it's a level game, it's a well leveled game, but with so many races. How did you face this challenge? How to level all these races? Yeah, well, we had a lot of playtesting to do and... actually, when was the time to find a publisher I met Uwe Rosenberg, and he brought us all together: Jens and Frank, he is the publisher now. So we have some playtests together and soon we... We decided it would be good if Jens would join in as co-designer because there was so much work to do with leveling all, balancing all the different factions and... - Creating new factions, and so the terrains. What could we choose for the new factions? What can I do? Maybe the Fakirs can fly on the carpet. Should be matched. Most important thing is, it must bring the feeling of fun to you, when you play this faction. That was how we looked when we tested it and... Is it fun to play this faction or that was boring? Is it challenging, or is it too easy? And how the other players feel? When someone play, maybe, the Fakir, how feel the others if he fly, over the board. - And take their lands, from behind. - It's OK or it's... - Is it too agressive? - Is it agressive for me, and took the fun from me to the game? So we canceled a lot of things. Yeah, I can imagine. You have so much fine-tuning of the game, I think. How was the process of developing this? Which stages it takes? First of all there was the basic elements of terraforming and upgrading structures into different kinds of buildings. And, of course, different factions but, the balancing and the differences in the factions, that was the last part of the game, which took almost the last two years of the developing process. And most of the fine-tunes we went was to balancing the races. We have workers, we have power, we have money, we have priests. We have the cult tracks. And we have all these gears... these wheels we had to fit together and... we have to turn the different wheels of the mechanics in the game so... - How long did you take? - Helge began 10 years ago, I think, with the first steps of the game. I joined to design the game... - 2010? - 2010, yes. Two years before it was published, Jens joined in and then we had the final balancing, which took 2 years. - And put the story into the game. Story in the rulebook to the factions , with (graphic) designer Dennis (Lohausen), the special look of the factions. - Ok. And the last question. What can we expect for the future? What are your plans, new games, new challenges for us gamers, please? Of course we are working on Terra Mystica expansion. Which will be published next year, I think. But we need, or needed, a lot of time to do the balancing for new races to fit in. Are you working together? - Yes, of course. We have other plans, but they are for the future. - It's right. - Is it on the same project, or do you have other projects too? - We work both... - Do you share other projects? - ... for the expansions. This expansion will have Acolytes, Frost Maidens... - Frost Maidens, Yetis. - Shapeshifters. - And riverwalkers. Six new faction were been included and new boards I think. - I can't wait. Thank you so much. It was my pleasure and for us all from Brazil. Thank you. - Thanks and bye bye. - Bye.
